question_text: Define heliophytes and sciophytes. Name a plant near you that is either a heliophyte or a sciophyte.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 13, book p.35, VSAQ 5. The book's wording is 'Name a plant from your locality'; it is kept in meaning but written as 'a plant near you' so no place is named (Rule 35). Both of the book's examples are kept: Helianthus for heliophyte and Funaria for sciophyte. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services · 2 marks

steps.label: Heliophytes
lines: Heliophytes: plants that grow well in
direct sunlight. They have small, thick
leaves and a high rate of photosynthesis
steps.why: Helios means sun, so a heliophyte is defined by the light level of its habitat — full, direct sunlight.
common_mistakes: Defining heliophytes by heat instead of light. The dividing factor is light, not temperature.
Leaving out the example. Each half of this question carries its own example.
steps.memory_tip: Helios = sun (as in helium, found in the sun). Heliophyte = sun plant.
steps.margin_note: One definition line plus one example is a full mark. Do not write more.

steps.label: Sciophytes

lines.text: Sciophytes: plants that grow in shade

lines: They grow in shady places under the shade
of taller plants, have broad thin leaves
steps.why: Skia means shade, so a sciophyte is the opposite habitat class to a heliophyte. Broad thin leaves catch more of the little light that reaches them.
common_mistakes: Spelling it as psychophyte or scyophyte. It is sciophyte, from skia meaning shade.
Saying sciophytes need no light. They need low light, not zero light.
steps.memory_tip: Two Greek roots, one pair: helios sun, skia shade.
steps.margin_note: The question says name A plant, so one example on either side is enough.

insider_note: This is a two-part definition, so a student who defines both and gives only one example usually loses half a mark. Give one example on each side.
